main.job: identity and description: say who or what someone or something is, and what it is like
main.why: The most-used verb in Italian; every sentence about who, what or what-like needs it.

main.job: existence: say that something is there / exists (plural ci sono)
main.why: English speakers say 'there is' constantly; Italian does it with c'è / ci sono, not with è alone.

spares.job: negation: put before the verb to make a sentence negative
spares.why: The next building-block job after identity and existence.

jobs_covered.people: not covered (pronoun set larger than count)
jobs_covered.want/can/must: not covered (modal set of 3 larger than count)

shape.notes: Count is 2, so only the two highest building blocks fit. Pronouns and modals are closed sets bigger than the count, so not started (R-SEL-04). Stare is treated as a separate verb (how you are, ongoing action), not a closed copula pair with essere in Italian.
